# Tabsets and layout {#sec-g-layout}

Layout tools keep a long chapter readable. Each example shows the rendered element, then its source, then when the house style uses it.

## Tabsets {#sec-g-layout-tabsets}

::: {.panel-tabset}
### Control

The control group has four samples. Its depth and filter results would go here.

#### A nested heading

Headings inside a tab stay inside that tab.

### Treated

The treated group has four samples. Its depth and filter results would go here.
:::

````markdown
::: {.panel-tabset}
### Control

The control group has four samples.

#### A nested heading

Headings inside a tab stay inside that tab.

### Treated

The treated group has four samples.
:::
````

Use it for one tab per group or per contrast, when the same figure repeats for each.

Do not use tabs when the reader must compare panels side by side. A tab hides every panel but one. Use a multi-panel figure instead (see @sec-g-figures).

## Margin notes {#sec-g-layout-margin}

The depth threshold was set before the data were seen.

::: {.column-margin}
The threshold and its date are recorded in Methods (@sec-methods).
:::

````markdown
::: {.column-margin}
The threshold and its date are recorded in Methods.
:::
````

Use it for a short aside that would break the flow of a paragraph.

## Footnotes {#sec-g-layout-footnotes}

Counts were converted to counts per million before plotting.[^cpm]

[^cpm]: Counts per million divides each count by the sample total and multiplies by one million.

````markdown
Counts were converted to counts per million before plotting.[^cpm]

[^cpm]: Counts per million divides each count by the sample total and multiplies by one million.
````

Use it for a definition or a source that most readers will not need.

## Details blocks {#sec-g-layout-details}

<details>
<summary>Full list of filter steps</summary>

1. Remove features with a mean count below the threshold.
2. Remove samples below the depth cut-off.
3. Recompute library sizes.

</details>

````markdown
<details>
<summary>Full list of filter steps</summary>

1. Remove features with a mean count below the threshold.
2. Remove samples below the depth cut-off.
3. Recompute library sizes.

</details>
````

Use it for a long list that supports a section but is not part of its argument.
